correctness.rationale: The age has strong amalgamation and independent one-point insertions in all d order coordinates, giving (m+1)^d ordinary base-fixed insertion slots. Its signed-coordinate overgroup quotient is C2 wr S_d; a fixed labeled base allows exactly those signed coordinate permutations matching ranking lists up to reversal, so for m>=2 the surviving quotient is product S_{r_i}. Reverse normalizing each class turns the slot action into independent multiset permutations, with orbits binom(m+r_i,r_i). The ratio binom(m+r,r)/binom(m+r-1,r-1)=(m+r)/r strictly decreases, proving the unique occupancy min/max patterns; all patterns are realized by free amalgamation. For m<=1 sign symmetries are transitive on slots. Independent direct stabilizer/slot enumeration checked 102 finite cases and 7 extremal configurations; no extrapolation used as proof.
